source.author: verg
source.text: Hinc Gaetulae urbes, genus insuperabile bello, et Numidae infreni cingunt et inhospita Syrtis; hinc deserta siti regio, lateque furentes Barcaei.
source.text_original: Hinc Gaetulae urbes, genus insuperabile bello, / et Numidae infreni cingunt et inhospita Syrtis; / hinc deserta siti regio, lateque furentes / Barcaei.
source.text_english: On this side the Gaetulian cities, a race unconquerable in war, and the unruly Numidians, and the inhospitable Syrtis encircle it; on this side a land desolate from thirst, and the Barcaei raging far and wide.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: hoc autem anno, cum tres explicassem libros, subitus impetus barbarorum, de quibus tuus dicit Uergilius: lateque uagantes Barcaei et sancta scriptura de Ismahel: contra faciem omnium fratrum suorum habitabit, sic Aegypti limitem, Palaestinae, Phoenices, Syriae percucurrit ad instar torrentis cuncta secum trahens, ut uix manus eorum misericordia Christi potuerimus euadere.
reuse.text_original: hoc autem anno, cum tres explicassem libros, subitus impetus barbarorum, de quibus tuus dicit Uergilius: lateque uagantes Barcaei et sancta scriptura de Ismahel: contra faciem omnium fratrum suorum habitabit, sic Aegypti limitem, Palaestinae, Phoenices, Syriae percucurrit ad instar torrentis cuncta secum trahens, ut uix manus eorum misericordia Christi potuerimus euadere.
reuse.text_english: But in this year, after I had finished three books, there was a sudden onslaught of the barbarians, of whom your Vergil says, and Holy Scripture of Ismahel, the Barcaei, wandering far and wide: he shall dwell in the face of all his brothers; and it rushed through the border of Egypt, Palestine, Phoenicia, and Syria like a torrent, dragging everything along with it, so that by the mercy of Christ we could scarcely escape their hands.
